title: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 12](/bible/2-samuel/12)

## Introduction

Chapter 12 brings the reckoning. The Most High sends Nathan, who tells David the parable of the rich man who took the poor man's one little ewe lamb; David's anger is kindled against the man, and Nathan answers, Thou art the man. The Most High recounts all He gave David and pronounces judgment: the sword shall never depart from his house, evil shall be raised up out of his own house, and the child shall die. David repents with godly sorrow, the child dies, and afterward Solomon is born, whom the Most High loved. This shows that David was judged; he did not get off scot-free, but because he had godly sorrow he was not put to death, and through that Solomon, and ultimately Christ, came.

**[2 Samuel 12:1-6](/bible/2-samuel/12#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/12#v1)</sup> And the Lord sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/12#v2)</sup> The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds:
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/12#v3)</sup> But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/12#v4)</sup> And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/12#v5)</sup> And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the Lord liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die:
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/12#v6)</sup> And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.

- The Most High sent Nathan unto David, who told him of two men in one city, one rich and one poor. The rich man had many flocks and herds, but the poor man had nothing save one little ewe lamb he had bought and nourished up, which was unto him as a daughter. When a traveler came, the rich man spared his own flock and took the poor man's lamb. David's anger was greatly kindled, and he said the man that had done this shall surely die and restore the lamb fourfold, because he had no pity.
- Nathan came to David with a parable. When David judged that the man deserved to die for taking the poor man's one lamb, he was unknowingly pronouncing sentence on himself.

**[2 Samuel 12:7-9](/bible/2-samuel/12#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/12#v7)</sup> And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/12#v8)</sup> And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/12#v9)</sup> Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the Lord, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.

- Nathan said unto David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the Most High: I anointed thee king over Israel, delivered thee out of the hand of Saul, gave thee thy master's house and wives, and the house of Israel and of Judah, and would have given thee more. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment to do evil, killing Uriah the Hittite with the sword and taking his wife, slaying him with the sword of the children of Ammon?
- The Most High said if David would have just asked, He would have given him anything, for He had already given him the kingdom, Saul's house, and protection from Saul. The commandment David despised was what was read in [Deuteronomy 27](/bible/deuteronomy/27). There is a term called suicide by cop; David committed murder by the hand of another nation, because he set the whole thing up.

**[2 Samuel 12:10-12](/bible/2-samuel/12#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/12#v10)</sup> Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/12#v11)</sup> Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/12#v12)</sup> For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.

- Thus saith the Most High: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house, because thou hast despised me and taken the wife of Uriah to be thy wife. Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes and give them unto thy neighbour, who shall lie with them in the sight of the sun. Thou didst it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun.
- As the four chapters go on, and beyond, you are going to see the fruition of what just happened worked out in David's own house.

**[2 Samuel 12:13-14](/bible/2-samuel/12#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/12#v13)</sup> And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said unto David, The Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/12#v14)</sup> Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.

- David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Most High. Nathan said the Most High hath also put away thy sin; thou shalt not die. Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Most High to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
- The judgment of David was that child being put to death. This goes back to Exodus 34: the Most High keeps mercy and forgives iniquity, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquities of the fathers upon the children. David got pardoned, but he did not get cleared; the punishment was still coming, one part the men of Israel dying in battle, the other his son having to die and his house having nothing but trouble.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 34:7](/bible/exodus/34#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/34#v7)</sup> Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

    The Most High keeps mercy and forgives iniquity, but will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children.

**[2 Samuel 12:15-23](/bible/2-samuel/12#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/12#v15)</sup> And Nathan departed unto his house. And the Lord struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/12#v16)</sup> David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/12#v17)</sup> And the elders of his house arose, and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/12#v18)</sup> And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/12#v19)</sup> But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/12#v20)</sup> Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the Lord, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/12#v21)</sup> Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/12#v22)</sup> And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether God will be gracious to me, that the child may live?
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-samuel/12#v23)</sup> But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.

- Nathan departed, and the Most High struck the child, so that it was very sick. David besought God for the child, fasted, and lay all night upon the earth, refusing to rise or eat with the elders of his house. On the seventh day the child died, and the servants feared to tell him. When David perceived by their whispering that the child was dead, he arose, washed, anointed himself, changed his apparel, worshiped in the house of the Most High, and then ate bread. When asked why, he said that while the child lived he fasted and wept, for who could tell whether God would be gracious; but now the child was dead, he could not bring him back, he would go to him but the child would not return to him.
- David did all the fasting and prayer before the child died because he knew it was of the Most High that this would happen; no amount of prayer would bring the child back. David was content, saying he did not want it to happen but had no choice in the matter, for the Most High had said it would be so.

**[2 Samuel 12:24-25](/bible/2-samuel/12#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/2-samuel/12#v24)</sup> And David comforted Bath–sheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the Lord loved him.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-samuel/12#v25)</sup> And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the Lord.

- David comforted Bathsheba his wife, went in unto her, and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon; and the Most High loved him, and sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, who called his name Jedidiah, because of the Most High.
- Through David's judgment, Solomon was still able to be born; it was all part of the plan of the Most High. The backup master plan behind everything was Christ, who still had to be born through David's lineage; David was still loved and still forgiven, which shows repentance, and that even the mighty among us can fall and yet rise back up.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Corinthians 7:10](/bible/2-corinthians/7#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/2-corinthians/7#v10)</sup> For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

    Godly sorrow worketh repentance unto salvation, but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
  - **[Psalm 119:120](/bible/psalms/119#v120)**
    > <sup>[120](/bible/psalms/119#v120)</sup> My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.

    My flesh trembleth for fear of thee, and I am afraid of thy judgments.
  - **[Proverbs 24:16](/bible/proverbs/24#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/proverbs/24#v16)</sup> For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.

    A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again.

**[2 Samuel 12:26-31](/bible/2-samuel/12#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/2-samuel/12#v26)</sup> And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-samuel/12#v27)</sup> And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/2-samuel/12#v28)</sup> Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/2-samuel/12#v29)</sup> And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/2-samuel/12#v30)</sup> And he took their king’s crown from off his head, the weight whereof was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was set on David’s head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/2-samuel/12#v31)</sup> And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.

- Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon and took the royal city, then sent for David to gather the rest of the people and take the city, lest it be called after Joab's name. David gathered all the people, went to Rabbah, took it, and took the king's crown of a talent of gold with the precious stones, and set it on his head. He brought forth great spoil, put the people to labor under saws and axes of iron and to the brickkiln, and did so unto all the cities of Ammon, then returned to Jerusalem.
- David won against the children of Ammon once again. What we gather from these four chapters is that David was called, he was king, a very mighty man, but he slipped and fell; he had godly sorrow, and in that godly sorrow he was not put to death. If he had been, there would be no Solomon, and through that no Christ. The only one perfect in this world was Christ, in whom there was no iniquity; but the men before us, when they failed, had godly sorrow, repented, and kept the commandments of the Most High even after they fell, rising back up again.
